Verifier notes and special checks

Inspection used only the printed page, the system crops, the crop-boundary overlays, and the geometry assist. Twenty-two complete bars are printed on one page, in four systems of five, six, six, and five bars. Each bar holds two quarter-note beats in 2/4. The upper staff opens in the treble clef and the lower staff in the bass clef. Those same clefs are reprinted at the start of the later systems, and no clef change is printed. One sharp is printed at the opening and reprinted later; the key does not change. A combined repeat stands between the eighth and ninth bars, and the piece ends with a repeat barline after the twenty-second bar. There is no pickup. Slurs, dynamics, and the ritardando remain inside the system crops.

  • System 1, first region: Is the first region a pickup? No. It is a complete bar of two quarter-note beats after the 2/4 signature.
  • System 2, between the eighth and ninth bars: Is the heavy barline one boundary or two bars? One boundary. Repeat dots sit on both sides of a thin stroke and a thick stroke.
  • System 4, close of the last bar: Do the thin and thick closing strokes add an extra bar? No. They are one final barline, with repeat dots on the left.
  • Crop edges of all four systems: Does any slur, dynamic, or the ritardando cross a crop edge? No. The ritardando stays inside the third system, and the slurs stay inside their systems.
